design_inputs.value: tolerate shaft misalignment up to 0.5 degrees, operate from minus 10 to 55 degrees C at belt speeds to 4.5 meters per second, and allow a single technician to replace the cartridge in under 20 minutes without removing the idler frame

Idler failure is preceded by a measurable causal precursor chain — dust ingress raises bearing friction torque, friction raises cartridge temperature, and both rise weeks before seizure. By instrumenting each idler with a self-powered torque/temperature node, the friction signature becomes an observable real-time state variable, so degradation is detected at the ingress stage rather than at failure, and replacement is triggered by measured condition, not by design-time guesses about seals and clearance.

proposed_design.input: tolerate shaft misalignment up to 0.5 degrees, operate from minus 10 to 55 degrees C at belt speeds to 4.5 meters per second, and allow a single technician to replace the cartridge in under 20 minutes without removing the idler frame

By instrumenting each idler with a self-powered torque/temperature node, the friction signature becomes an observable real-time state variable, so degradation is detected at the ingress stage rather than at failure, and replacement is triggered by measured condition, not by design-time guesses about seals and clearance.
